title: Monkey Patching and Its Risks
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of monkey patching and its risks in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply monkey patching and its risks in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to safer alternatives and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Monkey Patching and Its Risks through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding monkey patching and its risks helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Monkey Patching and Its Risks helps you reason about reopening classes. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Reopening classes. Then connect it to Method conflicts. The remaining syllabus points—Compatibility and testing risks, Safer alternatives—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports monkey patching and its risks. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for monkey patching and its risks using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Safer alternatives), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain monkey patching and its risks, identify its place in modules, mixins, and code organization, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
